title: Rooms of the Village
story: A text adventure is a map of rooms. Each room lists where its exits lead, and that is just a dictionary.
goal: Write go(room, direction): return the room you reach, or the same room if there is no exit that way. WORLD is given.
hints: WORLD[room] is a dictionary of exits. How do you look up one exit safely?
dict.get(key, default) returns the default when the key is missing.
socratic: What should happen when the exit does not exist?
Why is KeyError a bad way to handle a wall?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Rooms of the Village”?
